method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the fixed-input halting set and s-m-n reduction, with exact formula, macro, label and reference parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: K_1 as the set of programs halting on input zero, its c.e. status and the computable reduction K_0≤_m K_1.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section applies the preceding reducibility proposition. K_1 comprises indices e for which φ_e(0) is defined. It is c.e. through an existential T witness and is noncomputable if K_0 reduces to it.
samples.checks: The fixed input 0, definedness, two claims and both cross-references are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An oracle answering only whether a program halts on input 0 can still answer whether (e,x) belongs to K_0: build a program e_x that ignores any supplied input and simulates e on x, then ask whether e_x halts on 0. This transforms a K_0 question into a K_1 question without reversing yes/no.
samples.checks: The original pair (e,x), new program e_x, ignored arbitrary input, fixed 0 query and K_0-to-K_1 direction remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Define a three-place partial computable f(x,y,z)≃φ_x(y), independent of z, and choose e indexing f. The s-m-n theorem yields s(e,x,y) indexing a one-place program that ignores z and computes φ_x(y). Hence φ_s(e,x,y)(0) is defined iff φ_x(y) is, so the computable g(w)=s(e,(w)_0,(w)_1) reduces K_0 to K_1.
samples.checks: Arity, index e, all three variables, both partial equalities, input zero, code coordinates and g definition are preserved.
